{{Short description|American mathematician (1929–1997)}}
'''Donald W. Marquardt''' (March 13, 1929, New York City  – July 5, 1997,<ref name="QualityDigest"/> [[New Castle, Delaware]]) was an American statistician, the rediscoverer of the [[Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm|Levenberg–Marquardt nonlinear least squares fitting algorithm]].<ref name="NLSA">Paul Davis (1993). [http://202.38.126.65/mirror/www.siam.org/siamnews/mtc/mtc1093.htm Levenberg–Marquart Methods and Nonlinear Estimation] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090125074853/http://202.38.126.65/mirror/www.siam.org/siamnews/mtc/mtc1093.htm |date=January 25, 2009 }}, ''SIAM News'', Vol. 26, Number 6, October 1993.</ref>

Marquardt was educated at [[Columbia University]] with bachelor's degree in 1950 in physics and mathematics and at the [[University of Delaware]] with master's degree in 1956 in mathematics and statistics.<ref>{{citation|title=A Conversation with Donald Marquardt|first=Gerald J.|last=Hahn|journal=Statistical Science|volume=10|issue=4|date=November 1995|pages=377–393|jstor=2246136}}</ref> Marquardt joined [[DuPont]] in 1953 and worked there for 39 years. He also founded and managed the DuPont Quality Management & Technology Center.<ref name="QualityDigest">[http://www.qualitydigest.com/aug97/html/newsdig.html ''Quality Digest Magazine'', August 1997]</ref> In 1963 he published his famous paper "algorithm for least-squares estimation of nonlinear problems" in [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] journal. Marquardt developed his algorithm to solve fitting nonlinear chemical models to laboratory data.<ref name="NLSA"/> In 1975 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-08-20.</ref>

As manager of the DuPont Applied Statistics Group, he led development of the [[Quality Management|Product Quality Management methodology and computer systems]] that implemented the company's continuous improvement initiatives from the mid-1970s to the late 1990s.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Marquardt |first1=Donald W.|author2-link=Dana Ulery|last2=Ulery|first2=Dana L.|title=Product Quality Management |year=1991| publisher= E.I. du Pont de Nemours, Quality Management & Technology Center |location=Wilmington, DE | oclc=29224881 }}</ref> He won the [[Shewhart Medal]] in 1986.

In 1991, he established his own company, Donald W. Marquardt and Associates, which provides consulting and training in quality management, quality assurance, ISO 9000 standards, applied statistics, strategic planning and organizational change.<ref name="QualityDigest"/>

He died from a heart attack at the age of 68.<ref name="QualityDigest"/>

== Awards and achievements ==
* [[President of the American Statistical Association]] (1986)
* Elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].
* Leader of the U.S. delegation to the [[ISO 9000]] International Quality Standard writing group.
* [[American Society for Quality]] (ASQ) [[Shewhart Medal]] (1987)
* [[American Statistical Association]] Statistician of the Year (1993–94)
* [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]] (1995)
* [[American National Standards Institute]] Meritorious Service Award
